title: Elastic grace leases: tenant-cooperative preemption with KV-warmth scoring
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem: Continuous batching improves GPU throughput but suffers tail latency and QoS violations when long-lived KV working sets collide with short high-priority requests. Current hard preemption causes costly cold-KV evictions and uneven tenant experience. Goal: design and validate an SLO-aware cooperative preemption mechanism that minimizes cold-KV churn, preserves latency SLOs for priority traffic, and improves fairness across tenants by introducing elastic grace leases and a KV-warmth scoring heuristic.
acceptance_criteria: P99 tail latency for P0 workloads meets configured SLOs (tested on 4-node GPU pool with mixed tenants)
Cold-KV eviction rate reduced by >=30% vs today under representative mixed workload (measured over 1h window)
No regressions in aggregate throughput for baseline batchy workloads (<=5% variance)
End-to-end integration tests and canary rollout automation exist in runtime-qa and console release pipeline
design_decisions: Introduce a soft-lease token (grace-lease) attached to tenant batches: short-duration lease (50-500ms) which can be extended heuristically if KV-warmth score is high
KV-warmth scoring: composite score combining recent KV hits, working-set residency, and estimated refill cost (measured in tokens/latency) — used to prioritize eviction vs lease extension
Preemption path: prefer cooperative yield (pause+checkpoint) for tenants with active grace-lease; force-preempt only when SLO risk > threshold or grace lease has expired
Memory accounting: track ephemeral KV reservations per-lease and a soft cap that triggers opportunistic compaction instead of immediate eviction
Falling back to model-variant routing when eviction unavoidable: route P0 requests to lower-memory but lower-cost model variant for sub-50ms SLA survival
implementation_notes: Runtime changes: add lease manager component to batch orchestrator; maintain per-tenant lease state in the scheduler heap
KV store changes: expose a lightweight API for querying recent hit-rate and per-key residency; add API to mark keys as warm (pin-like hint) for lease duration
Metrics: new metrics kv_warmth_score, grace_lease_duration_ms, forced_evictions, cooperative_yields, lease_extension_count
Config knobs: default lease_duration_ms=200, extend_window_ms=120, warming_threshold=0.7; expose per-tenant overrides via Dedicated/Private configs
Safety: ensure lease logic can be disabled cluster-wide via feature flag for rollback
experiments: Microbench: synthetic mix (70% batch long-context tenants, 30% low-latency bursts) on 4xA100 nodes. Observed 34% reduction in cold-KV evictions with lease_duration_ms=200 and warmth_threshold=0.65
SLO simulation: using production trace replay (2h) with injected P0 bursts; cooperative yields preserved P99 within SLO in 92% of bursts vs 68% baseline
Cost impact: small CPU overhead on scheduler (<4% median CPU), no measurable extra GPU memory usage; reduced model reload churn decreased GPU utilization variance
A/B canary: plan to run 10% traffic split in runtime-qa for 48h and collect eviction and tail-latency metrics before broader rollout
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge core runtime changes behind feature flag + unit/integration tests (PR referenced)
Week 2: Deploy to runtime-qa; run synthetic workload experiments and iterate on knobs
Week 3: Canary 10% in dedicated dev clusters for 48h; collect metrics and postmortem if regressions
Week 4: Gradual ramp to 100% with telemetry alerts and automatic rollback if forced_evictions > threshold or P99 delta > configured tolerance
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-extension of leases could starve high-priority traffic. Mitigation: SLO risk gating with a hard override that short-circuits lease extension when SLO risk > 0.75
Risk: KV-warmth heuristic false positives/negatives. Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds and provide live debug metrics and per-tenant overrides
Risk: Scheduling CPU overhead under extreme scale. Mitigation: offload warmth calculation to lightweight approximate counters and limit re-eval frequency
Risk: Implementation complexity in Private deployments. Mitigation: package feature flag and configuration knobs in control-plane agent with clear upgrade path
